19.05.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
03.
1.

This is the second successive bail application under section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the petitioner in connection with Badachana P.S. Case No. 115 of 2018 corresponding to C.T. Special (POCSO) Case No. 60 of 2018 pending in the Court of learned Addl. Adhoc Special (POCSO) Judge,
Jajpur.
He is facing trial for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(ii) of the IPC and read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
2. The earlier bail application of the petitioner BLAPL No. 10487 of 2019 had been dismissed on 02.11.2021 by this Court.

While disposing of the applications it was observed that since the petitioner appeared to be in custody since 3 years, the learned trial Court should complete the trial expeditiously, if not already completed.
3. The allegations in brief against the petitioner are that while the victim a 7 years old girl was playing, the petitioner took her to a nearby pond and committed rape on her.

4. Mr. R.K. Routray, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 07.06.2018 and although the trial has started, out of 18 charge sheet witnesses, only 3 charge sheet witnesses have been examined so far which includes the victim, her mother and her aunt.
He has filed copies of their depositions.
He further submits that the petitioner was very young being aged Khetrabasi Mallik @ Rinku vs State Of Odisha .....

about 21 years at the time of incident and in the meanwhile, he has stayed almost five years in custody for which the informant has no objection if the petitioner is released on bail.
His further submission is that apart from slapping the informant he has not caused any other injury which would be evident from the medical examination report and the evidence of the witnesses.
Keeping in view the right of the petitioner to speedy trial, the petitioner may be released on bail.

5. Mr. D. Nayak, learned Addl. Govt. Advocate for the State opposes the prayer for bail stating that the victim in the case was aged about 7 years at the time of occurrence and only because of the timely arrival of her mother and aunt, she was rescued before she could suffer further harm.

He also submits that the victim and her mother have supported the prosecution case while deposing in Court and no indulgence should be shown to the petitioner, as incidents of sexual assaults on minors is increasing every day and it would send a wrong signal if the petitioner is granted bail.

His further submission is that in view of the nature of allegations against the petitioner and the age of the victim, her evidence and the decision of the Supreme Court, there is no scope of settling the matter on compromise.

6. Waiving notice, Mr. P.C. Sejpada, learned counsel has appeared on behalf of the informant-opposite party no.2 and has filed an affidavit stating that since the petitioner is in custody since 07.06.2018 and the matter has been amicably settled among the families and they are living peacefully in a friendly atmosphere she has no objection if the petitioner is released on bail.
He also submits that the informant is present in Court.

7. The opposite party no.2 identified by Mr. Sejpada, learned counsel appears in Court and submits that since the accused has stayed in custody for almost five years, she has no objection if he released on bail.
She has also stated that the victim is attending school.

8. Perused the medical report of the victim produced by the learned State Counsel along with the case diary and the depositions of the victim, her mother and her aunt which have been annexed to the bail application.

9. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the respective parties and especially the fact that the petitioner is in custody since almost five years and 15 charge sheet witnesses still remain to be examined, I am inclined to allow this application for bail.
10. Let the petitioner- Khetrabasi Mallik @ Rinku be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be fixed by the learned Court below in seisin over the matter, including the following conditions:
( i) He will not establish any contact with the victim girl or her relatives or go near their house.
(ii) He will not threaten or try to influence prosecution witnesses while on bail.
